I'm 45 years old, been farming these fields in Quzhou County since I was a boy. I only finished primary school, but I know my land better than any book. My family has 8 mu of flat, good soil on the North China Plain. Every year I watch what my neighbors do — Old Wang down the road, my cousin Li — and I mostly follow them because they know what works, and if I try something strange and it fails, my family goes hungry.

This year, like last year, I'm planting winter wheat on all 8 mu in October. It's what everyone here does. Wheat gives us grain to eat and some cash to buy other things, and the government sets a minimum purchase price so I won't get cheated. I'll buy improved seed from the agricultural supply shop in town — not the most expensive kind, but the same kind most of the village uses. Before planting I'll rotary till the ground to break it up. I'll put down compound fertilizer, about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu plus some phosphorus and potash. My neighbor tried cutting back on fertilizer two years ago and his wheat came up thin and yellow, so I'm not taking that chance. I'd rather spend the money than lose the crop. I'll irrigate four times from the tube well: at planting to get it germinated, then at green-up in spring, at jointing, and at grain filling. The pumping costs me, but dry wheat is worthless around here.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I have to move fast — maybe four or five days at most — to get summer maize in the ground before the rainy season passes. I'm planting hybrid maize seed on the same 8 mu. Saved seed doesn't yield enough, so I always buy hybrid from the shop even though it's more expensive. I'll put down another round of fertilizer, about 16 kg nitrogen per mu. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat because summer rains usually help, but if the rain doesn't come I'll irrigate twice — once when the plants are knee-high and once when they tassel. I'll spray for weeds and bugs twice. I know some people talk about saving water and using less fertilizer, but I've got my wife, my two kids, and my old mother to feed. Last year when I cut back on inputs, I lost money. I'd rather be safe and make sure there's food on the table.
